Campaign brief: Before public traffic puts auth email under pressure, Resend gives the engineer a separate transactional sending route they can connect through custom SMTP and test deliberately; Supabase’s own Auth rate limit remains a separate setting they must adjust.
events.reader:
Selected audience: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does.
Situation context (grounded; check applicability): Individual engineers integrating a hosted auth platform (Supabase Auth) into a product's signup, password-reset, invite, and OTP flows post first-person accounts, in GitHub issues and discussions on the platform's own repos, of hitting the built-in email rate limit and having to reason through Supabase's dashboard logs, SMTP settings, and plan tiers themselves to diagnose it.
events.reader_segment: The one backend engineer at a ten-person product team who owns email because nobody else does
events.promise: Before public traffic puts auth email under pressure, Resend gives the engineer a separate transactional sending route they can connect through custom SMTP and test deliberately; Supabase’s own Auth rate limit remains a separate setting they must adjust.
events.arc: Announce Resend, connect its relevance to the production-readiness moment, show the concrete SMTP route and its boundary, then invite the reader to evaluate it before launch traffic arrives.

emails.job: Announce Resend and get the reader to evaluate it as the custom SMTP route for auth email before a launch or usage increase exposes the built-in sender’s limits.
emails.single_idea: Resend is now available as a transactional email platform the reader can connect to Supabase Auth through custom SMTP, giving auth messages a dedicated sending route that can be configured and evaluated before public traffic arrives.
emails.objection: Connecting another sender before launch may appear to create more work than continuing with the built-in option.
must_not_say: Do not promise that Resend changes or bypasses Supabase’s own Auth rate limit; it must still be adjusted separately.
Do not claim that Resend detects, prevents, or survives an Auth Hook clearing Supabase’s stored SMTP configuration.
Do not claim that Resend explains how Supabase counts messages against its own rate limit.
Do not imply that the free Resend plan removes sending ceilings; it is limited to 100 emails per day.
Do not promise complete isolation between transactional and marketing sending; both can exist on Resend, and IP-level isolation requires an eligible Scale plan with a dedicated IP.
Do not generalize Raycast’s 30-minute waitlist-email test into a guaranteed full migration time.
Do not lead with generic category claims such as modern email, simple sending, or better deliverability.
Do not broaden the email into Broadcasts, Automations, Templates, security, compliance, dedicated IPs, enterprise support, or the full SDK list.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.why_it_fails: Upgrading the hosted platform’s subscription does not itself replace the built-in sender or raise its email threshold. The engineer must configure an external SMTP provider and adjust the platform’s separate Auth rate limit.
emails.mechanism: Resend exposes documented SMTP credentials using smtp.resend.com and a Resend API key. Supabase accepts those credentials under its custom SMTP settings, while its Auth rate limit remains separately configurable in the dashboard.
emails.call_to_action: Sign up for free (create a free account) -> https://resend.com/signup
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend should become the custom SMTP provider for the product’s Supabase Auth email.
emails.next_step_value: Create an account, obtain the Resend credentials needed for SMTP configuration, and evaluate the route against the product’s auth-email requirements.
emails.next_step_limit: Signing up does not adjust Supabase’s separate Auth rate limit, prove production deliverability, or establish the time required for a complete migration.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: A low-risk reason to evaluate Resend now is its test mode: the engineer can exercise delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without sending real email to real recipients or affecting domain reputation.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Resend provides test mode and dedicated recipient addresses for simulating delivery, bounce, and spam-complaint events, with API and SDK paths available for the integration.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another sender appears to require exposing real recipients or committing production auth traffic. After: a bounded event-handling test can be run before making that production decision.
must_not_say: Do not claim a test proves production deliverability, throughput, or Supabase compatibility.
Do not claim test mode exercises the final SMTP route when the chosen test uses only the API.
Do not promise that Resend detects or survives Supabase clearing its SMTP configuration.
Do not imply that simulated events constitute a complete migration.
alternative_arguments.objection: Switching sending providers mid-product sounds like a project the engineer does not have time to begin.
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Sign up for free (create a free account) -> https://resend.com/signup
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend’s event and integration workflow is suitable for a limited pre-production evaluation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Create an account and run a bounded test of delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without sending to real recipients.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: This test does not validate production deliverability, the final Supabase SMTP route, or the effort required for a complete migration.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the launch around a safe first test for auth email, not broad claims about simplicity, speed, or deliverability.

events.subject: Resend for Supabase custom SMTP
events.preview_text: Configure a separate route before auth traffic tests the built-in sender.
events.body:
Resend is now available as a transactional email platform you can connect to Supabase Auth through custom SMTP. It gives signup confirmations, OTPs, magic links, and invites a separate sending route to evaluate before traffic increases.

The setup uses documented SMTP credentials: `smtp.resend.com`, username `resend`, an approved port, and your Resend API key as the password. Add them under Supabase Authentication settings after verifying your sending domain with Resend.

Supabase’s Auth rate limit remains separate. After saving custom SMTP, adjust it under Authentication > Rate Limits for the volume your product requires. Resend does not change that setting.

Create a free account to obtain the SMTP credentials and decide whether Resend fits your auth-email requirements.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "What Auth logs cannot test"
events.subject: What Auth logs cannot test
events.preview_text: Exercise delivery, bounce, and complaint events before changing production.
events.body:
Checking Supabase Auth logs can help trace a 429 rate-limit response. It does not provide a safe way to exercise delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events for a separate sender.

Resend is now available as an email-sending platform for developers, with custom SMTP and official SDK paths for transactional messages.

Before directing real auth messages through it, use Resend’s test recipient addresses to generate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events. Inspect the results in the Dashboard, Webhooks, and API **without sending to real recipients or affecting your domain reputation**.

This is a bounded event-handling test, not a production validation. Supabase’s Auth rate limit remains a separate setting to adjust, and an API test does not exercise the final SMTP route.

Create a free account.

emails.next_step_limit: The quota page does not establish production deliverability, complete migration effort, or whether the hosted auth platform's separate SMTP and rate-limit settings have been configured correctly.

events.subject: Resend for application-triggered email
events.preview_text: Check the documented Free allowance before configuring custom SMTP.
events.body:
Resend is now available to send your application’s transactional email through a dedicated provider. Connect through SMTP or an official SDK, with documented limits you can review before configuration.

For authentication email, this provides a route beyond a hosted platform’s built-in sender. Resend can handle the sending path, while the authentication platform’s separate SMTP and rate-limit settings still need to be configured there.

The Free plan includes **100 transactional emails per day and 3,000 per month**. Exceed the daily quota and Resend returns a 429; you can upgrade or wait for the quota to reset at midnight UTC.

Compare that allowance with your expected transactional-email volume. You can decide whether Free fits or whether to evaluate a paid plan before signing up and verifying a domain.

events.preview_text: Simulate delivery, bounce, and complaint events before configuring a production route.
events.body:
A provider evaluation should not require sending test messages to real people. Resend provides test addresses that simulate delivered, bounced, and spam-complaint events without affecting your domain reputation.

Resend is now available as an email sending platform for developers, connecting application-triggered messages through SMTP or official SDKs.

Send to delivered@resend.dev, bounced@resend.dev, and complained@resend.dev. These simulations let you exercise Resend’s Dashboard, Webhooks, and API together before configuring a real transactional-email route.

The Free plan allows **100 transactional emails per day and 3,000 per month**. Check that boundary against expected authentication and notification volume before investing setup time.

This test does not validate production deliverability, production volume, or your hosted authentication platform’s SMTP and rate-limit configuration. It gives you a bounded way to inspect the event path first.
